literal_meaning: পাত চাটা (leaf or plate to lick)
figurative_meaning_en: To flatter or bootlick in order to gain favor
example_sentences_in_bangla: সে তার উপরের পাত চাটা করে সুবিধা পেতে চায়।
রাজনীতিতে অনেকে পাত চাটা করে উন্নতি করে।
example_sentences_in_english: He bootlicks his superior to gain advantages.
In politics, many advance by flattering those in power.
history: This idiom likely originates from traditional Bengali eating practices where food was served on banana leaves (pata), and licking the leaf clean symbolized eagerness or appreciation, metaphorically extended to fawning behavior for favors.
note: The idiom reflects cultural norms around humility and hierarchy in Bengali society.
